newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-BARCELONA FACE FIORENTINA IN CUP WINNERS' CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA FACE FIORENTINA IN CUP WINNERS' CUP.

text.p: Three-times champions Barcelona will meet Fiorentina in the semifinals of this season's Cup Winners' Cup while holders Paris St Germain take on Liverpool.
Friday's draw pitted the Catalans, 15-8 favourites for the title, against the team which won the inaugural Cup Winners' Cup final back in 1961.
Barcelona won the cup in 1979, 1982 and 1989. Fiorentina, quoted as 11-4 third-favourites by British bookmakers Ladbrokes, have never repeated their early triumph.

"Last night was a big shock and today was an even bigger one," Fiorentina general manager Gianfranco Antognoni said after the draw, referring to the Italians' shock 1-0 home defeat by Benfica in the second leg of the quarter-finals.
"Barcelona are one of the greatest teams in the world and Ronaldo is one of the greatest players. It will be very difficult."
Holders PSG, who won their first-ever European title last season, face a Liverpool side chasing the only major trophy to have eluded them.
Liverpool have not appeared in a European final since the ill-fated Heysel stadium disaster of 1985 which led to a ban on English clubs playing in continental cup competitions.
"We're back among the big boys of Europe and that's where we belong," the club's veteran midfielder John Barnes said.
"When Liverpool dominated (in England) in the late 1980s we were not allowed in Europe and people were probably asking 'what happened to Liverpool?'
"This is really the first time since 1990 that we've been equipped to do well in Europe."
PSG general manager Jean-Francois Domergue said his club was daunted but thrilled to be drawn to play at Liverpool's Anfield stadium.
"It's clearly going to be a very difficult match. We'll be playing in one of the games mythic stadiums but when you see the four teams left in the cup it wouldn't have mattered who we drew."
In the UEFA Cup, Internazionale, chasing their third title in the competition in the 1990s, face a tough tie against French league leaders Monaco.
"That's the most talented of the three teams that we could have drawn but if we have any hope for the final we would have had to beat them anyway," Monaco sporting director Henri Biancheri said.
"But the good thing for us is that even playing away it will almost be like playing at home."
Spain's Tenerife face Schalke of Germany in the other semifinal.
The European Cup semifinal fixtures were decided by Wednesday night's quarter-final results.
Champions Juventus face 1995 winners Ajax Amsterdam in a repeat of last year's final while Manchester United take on Borussia Dortmund.
A separate draw on Friday gave Dortmund and Ajax home advantage in the first legs, due to be played on Wednesday April 9. The return legs are scheduled for April 23.
UEFA and Cup Winners' Cup matches will be played in the same weeks.
